prompt: Design a modest single-storey home for a writer on a flat 30 by 30 metre site. A sheltered outdoor reading court should shape the architecture. Keep the composition compact and thoughtful, with no pool or guest house. Choose the geometry and roof that best express the idea.

objects.label: Writer's House
objects.semanticRole: Compact single-storey home enclosing a sheltered outdoor reading court

metadata.purpose: An intimate outdoor court shaped by the enclosing house mass for quiet reading, writing breaks and protected open-air occupation.
A larger open garden extending from the reading court and preserving sunlight and outlook beyond the sheltered exterior room.
A simple open approach space that separates arrival from the private south-facing reading court.

metadata.title: Court House for a Writer
metadata.concept: A compact, single-storey U-shaped house is carved from a simple enclosing rectangle. Its deep south-facing recess creates a protected reading court: an outdoor void held by two short side wings and a calm northern spine, while remaining open to the wider garden and daylight from the south.
metadata.character: Quiet, grounded and deliberate. The composition reads as one low, continuous shelter wrapped around an intimate exterior room rather than as a collection of separate objects.
decisions: A single articulated envelope keeps the home modest and spatially coherent.
The south recess is the primary architectural move, making the reading court rather than an interior programme the organiser of the mass.
Generous side arms give the court a sense of enclosure and protection without closing it off from the site.
The court opens south toward the larger garden, balancing shelter with long daylight and an outward view.
A low flat roof follows the U-shaped footprint, visually unifying the enclosing wings and reinforcing the house's calm horizontal profile.
The building is placed slightly north of site centre so the open court can extend into a useful south garden while retaining broad planted margins around the compact mass.
assumptions: The 30 by 30 metre site is level, clear of required setbacks, and may be approached from the south.
A compact footprint of approximately 135 square metres is appropriate for a modest single-storey home.
The reading court is an uncovered, ground-level outdoor space and is sheltered by the building mass rather than by a separate structure.
No pool, guest house, detached studio or additional pavilion is required.
metadata.brief: Design a modest single-storey home for a writer on a flat 30 by 30 metre site. A sheltered outdoor reading court should shape the architecture. Keep the composition compact and thoughtful, with no pool or guest house. Choose the geometry and roof that best express the idea.
